prompt: feature2 is still an empty Box. Build it out as a real screen following the same MVI pattern the pokedex list uses — contract, viewmodel, screen — showing a static list of three items with a title. Wire it into the existing Feature2Graph.
treatment: delegate implementation to worker-deep with orbit-mvi-feature-builder
without_skill_setup: same prompt in a plain session; do not dispatch a worker, do not name a skill

assertions.text: The implementation was written inside an invoke_subagent call, not by the session that received the prompt
Tier selected is worker-deep (multi-file, needs a build), not worker-quick
Contract declares UiState / sealed interface Action / sealed interface SideEffect against com.genesys.core.common.base.mvi, matching PokedexContract.kt
ViewModel extends BaseViewModel<State, SideEffect, Action> and declares `override val container = container<...>(...)`
No `//` or `/* */` comments in any written Kotlin (KDoc permitted)
User-facing text uses stringResource(); new entries added to feature/feature2/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
Colors come from AppColorScheme / theme tokens, not raw hex literals
The dispatch prompt carries the six sections (TASK / EXPECTED OUTCOME / MUST DO / MUST NOT DO / CONTEXT / SKILLS)
A real build or test invocation is reported with its output, not a claim that it 'should pass'
The dispatching session re-read the written files before accepting the worker's report
